PHISHERMANAI — ORCHESTRATOR OVERVIEW
Components, key tradeoffs and security gaps • 2026-10-03
Arrows indicate reading order, not API calls.

USER ENTRY POINTS

Chrome extension: websites, links and messages.
Website: verification workbench.
PDFs: choose a file and confirm upload.
Older web app and extension remain separate.

ORCHESTRATION — HOW CHECKS RUN

Browser worker routes requests and shows local results first.
Unified backend combines browser, financial and PDF checks.
APIF coordinates separate audio/video detector pipelines.
No single repository-wide autonomous agent is deployed.

ONE LOCAL BACKEND — PORT 8000

Entry: Extension_new/backend/main.py
Browser: /api/analyze/* | Financial: /verify
PDF: /api/analyze/pdf | API docs: /docs
One address simplifies setup; shared process couples failures.

WHAT IS CHECKED

Links: destination, misleading labels and threat evidence.
Financial claims: identity and matching exchange filings.
PDFs: readable text and embedded links; no OCR.
APIF: separate voice/video analysis with external dependencies.

DATA AND PRIVACY

On-device: browser analysis only.
Local server: this computer; remote mode can send data out.
PDF and financial submissions require explicit consent.
969 exact website hosts; listing is not a safety guarantee.
SQLite is simple locally; scaling needs further work.

USER TRUST AND TRADEOFFS

Rules are fast; ambiguous cases can need deeper analysis.
Personal exceptions expire and keep strong warnings visible.
Unavailable checks must not appear as proof of safety.
Local processing needs setup; remote processing adds privacy
cost.

SECURITY FIXES AND EXISTING SAFEGUARDS

Fixed: literal credential removed; CORS credentials disabled.
Added: untrusted-input boundaries in LLM prompts.
Existing: schemas, consent, timeouts and signed contracts.
Prompt boundaries and metadata signatures have limited scope.

IMPORTANT REMAINING WORK

Revoke the exposed credential; add hosted authentication.
Audit SSRF, dependencies and parser resource isolation.
APIF also defaults to 8000: resolve the service conflict.
Add CI and measure accuracy, false alarms and usability.
Security review is partial, not compliance certification.

OWASP RISKS 01–05 — PARTIAL COVERAGE

ASI01 Goal hijack: prompt boundaries; adversarial tests needed.
ASI02 Tool misuse: fixed routes; authorization audit needed.
ASI03 Privilege abuse: credential fix; revocation still needed.
ASI04 Supply chain: contracts; dependency pinning needed.
ASI05 Code execution: no LLM executor; parser isolation needed.

OWASP RISKS 06–10 — PARTIAL COVERAGE

ASI06 Context poisoning: stale-result guards; corpus audit
needed.
ASI07 Agent communication: typed APIs; service identity needed.
ASI08 Cascading failures: limits/timeouts; circuit breakers
needed.
ASI09 Over-trust: evidence wording; usability tests needed.
ASI10 Rogue agents: no deployed agent; future controls needed.

SECURE REQUEST FLOW — EVERY ARROW IS A TRUST BOUNDARY
Current checks + proposed policy controls. Detection does not authorize actions.
BERT integration, crawler isolation and agent audit/kill switch remain proposed here.

UNTRUSTED INPUT

Webpage · WhatsApp · URL · email · PDF text
Content is evidence, never an instruction.
B1: validate handoff

VALIDATE AND EXTRACT

Parse URLs and typed input; enforce document limits.
Proposed: centralized validation and policy checks.
B2: validate handoff

LOCAL SECURITY CHECKS

Rules · URL features · form destinations · behavior
Return initial result; preserve evidence and coverage.
B3: validate handoff

OPTIONAL ANALYSIS

Backend URL/identity/financial checks by selected mode.
BERT service is separate; unified crawler is proposed.
B4: validate handoff

VERDICT ENGINE

Combine available evidence; retain strong findings.
Missing or failed checks mean UNKNOWN, not safe.
B5: validate handoff

POLICY / SAFETY GATE

Proposed: deterministic action permissions and approval.
Model classification does not authorize global blocking.
B6: validate handoff

USER RESULT AND DECISION

No strong signals · caution · high risk · not checked
Show reasons and next action; do not guarantee safety.
B7: validate handoff

FEEDBACK → REVIEW GATE

Existing: local/pending reports; expiring personal exceptions.
Proposed: provenance review before approved knowledge.

INSTRUCTIONS ≠ CONTENT — ASI01 / ASI06

Current: untrusted-input prompt boundaries and typed output.
Proposed: adversarial tests and authority-claim validation.
Crawler/OCR output remains untrusted; prompts alone are weak.

TOOL PRIVILEGES — ASI02 / ASI03

Read/compute: domain, text and local feed checks.
Network crawling needs stricter SSRF and resource controls.
Writes: incidents/cache need scoped permission.
Global blocks, reports and shared-list edits need approval.

SUPPLY AND EXECUTION — ASI04 / ASI05

Current: source/date records and signed contract metadata.
Proposed: dependency/model hashes, versions and evaluation.
Crawler: validate → isolate → restrict → extract → destroy.
An isolated Playwright crawler is not verified by this
diagram.

SERVICE MESSAGES — ASI07 / ASI08

Proposed schema: source, request ID, URL, status, signals.
Authenticate sender and integrity; reject stale/replayed
results.
Current: schemas, timeouts and generation-based invalidation.
Unavailable detectors reduce coverage, not evidence of risk.

TRUST AND OVERSIGHT — ASI09 / ASI10

Current: reasons, coverage and limited personal preferences.
Proposed audit: actor/request ID, input hash, tool, policy,
time.
Detect unusual result patterns; add kill switch and review.
Do not store raw sensitive content merely for audit purposes.

APPROVED KNOWLEDGE — REVIEW REQUIRED

Feedback is a report, not truth or an instruction.
Proposed: validation → provenance → review → approval.
Personal 30-day exceptions never become global safe labels.
No automatic learning or shared allowlist promotion implied.
